chunks: And from Musaddad bin Mustawrid, who said: Hammad bin Zayd narrated to me, from Mujalid, from Masrooq, who said:

We were sitting with Ibn Mas'ood after the sunset prayer, and he was teaching us the Qur'an. A man asked him, saying: 'O Abu Abdurrahman, did you ask the Prophet how many caliphs this umma will have?'
He said: 'No one asked me about this since I arrived in Iraq. Yes.' And he said: 'Your caliphs are twelve, in the number of the chieftains of the Children of Israel.'
ai.seo_question: How many caliphs did the Prophet say the Muslim umma would have?
ai.summary: This narration from Kitab al-Ghayba highlights the foundational Shia belief in the twelve divinely appointed successors, linking the prophetic prediction directly to the twelve chieftains (anbiya' or ru'asa') of the Children of Israel mentioned in the Quran. It serves as a critical Sunni-Shia convergent proof (tawatur) for the number of Imams, emphasizing that this specific count was a known tradition among early companions like Ibn Mas'ood.
